title: What is known about 1RB0LC_1LA1RE_1LD1RE_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_0RB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LC_1LA1RE_1LD1RE_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_0RB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open; analysis only begun. Sampled when the head is in C at the left end, the tape is mostly X(n, t) = C> 000 (100)^n T or Y(n, t) = C> (100)^n T, with a tail bit t (T = 1 or 101). X(n) goes to X((3n+5)/2) when n is odd and to Y((3n+6)/2) when n is even. Y(n) with n even goes to X((3n+4)/2). These single-number rules match every applicable event of the run from blank tape up to 4·1010 steps. Y(n) with n odd instead starts a nested phase with a second number y ≈ 3n/2, which ends when its successor is even and nests deeper otherwise. Those rules, and with them the halting condition, are further work. No halt was found from small X/Y starts.
Third pass. No halt in 1018 steps (macro simulation); no pushdown certificate with a DFA of at most 6 states on either side.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The single-number rules, against the run from blank tape
claims.text: X(n, t) → X((3n+5)/2, t') for odd n and → Y((3n+6)/2, t') for even n, with t' = t xor [n mod 4 ∈ {0, 1}]; Y(n, t) → X((3n+4)/2, t xor [n mod 4 = 0]) for even n. The 21 X/Y-events of the blank run up to 4·1010 steps that follow an X-event or an even Y-event are exactly as predicted (from X(5) at step 184 to X(75,654) at step 30,906,054,124). The one odd Y-event, Y(33,621) at step 6.1·109, went through the nested phase C> 000 (10)^2 (010)^50433 1, C> (100)^3 (010)^50432 01 and came back as X(75,654) = X(3·50,432/2 + 6).

claims.title: No halt from small single-number starts
claims.text: Direct runs of 10<sup>8</sup> steps from X(n, t) and Y(n, t) for n < 40 and both tails: none halts. Several of them go through nested phases two or three levels deep, e.g. from Y(3) and Y(7).

claims.title: Nested phases in closed form for 3 residues of 4
claims.text: From Y(n, t) with n odd: n = 4i+1 goes to X(9i+9, t xor [i odd]) after 5 left-end moments, n = 8i+7 to X(27i+36, t xor [i odd]) after 8; n = 8i+3 nests deeper (9 to 13 moments, e.g. Y(3) → X(22), Y(27) → Y(119)). Every odd n < 400, both tails, returns to the single-number form without halting.

claims.title: Relabelled mirror images among the holdouts
claims.text: Mirroring and renaming states turns this table into the ones of 1RB1LC_1LA0RD_0LB1LF_1RE1LC_1LC0RB_0LA--- (G02) and 1RB1LC_1LC0RF_0LF1LD_0LE---_1RF1LC_1LE0RA (G06); only the start state differs, so the rules hold there in mirror image.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>18</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, whole runs of equal blocks crossed at once, exact step counts) runs 10<sup>18</sup> steps from blank tape without a halt.
claims.where: holdouts/1RB0LE_0RC1RC_0RD1LA_1LD0LA_1LF1LC_---0LA/py/check_msim.py run 1RB0LC_1LA1RE_1LD1RE_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_0RB--- 1e18 (macro simulator c/msim.c there, checked against the direct simulator at 109 steps by check_msim.py check)

claims.title: No pushdown certificate with a DFA of at most 6 states
claims.text: The pushdown reduction of bb6-1RB0LF_1RC0LB/c/pds.c (one side of the tape kept exactly, the other abstracted by a DFA, reachability by post* saturation) reaches a halt for every DFA with at most 6 states, on either side: TM=1RB0LC_1LA1RE_1LD1RE_1RE0LA_0RA1RF_0RB--- ./pds 6 L and R.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The nested phase is the 3/2 map run on a second number until a parity test ends it; n = 8i+3 needs the next level, so the complete map is a recursion on the 2-adic digits of n. No synthetic nested phase with n < 400 halts.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LC_1LA0RD_0LB1LF_1RE1LC_1LC0RB_0LA--- up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1LC_1LC0RF_0LF1LD_0LE---_1RF1LC_1LE0RA up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Not known yet. Most of the time the machine runs a simple Collatz-like map, multiplying a number n by about 3/2 at each pass. When a parity test comes out the wrong way, it opens a nested phase with a second number, which can nest again. How it could halt, if it ever does, is hidden in those nested phases.

facts.text: No halt in the macro simulator (checked against the direct one at 10<sup>9</sup>).
The single-number map, matched against the run from blank tape up to 4·10<sup>10</sup> steps.
No halt, proved in Lean (first 10,000 by the kernel).

sections.heading: A 3/2 map with nested phases
html: When the head is in state C at the left end, the tape is usually X(n) = 000 (100)^n T or Y(n) = (100)^n T, with a short tail T = 1 or 101 that flips according to n mod 4.

From blank tape: X(5), X(10), Y(18), X(29), X(46), Y(72), X(110), Y(168), X(254), …, X(22,412), Y(33,621). Y(33,621) has an odd count, so a second number, 50,433 copies of 010, appears; it is followed by 50,432 copies, which is even, and the phase ends at X(75,654) at step 3.1·1010. When the second number is odd as well, the phase nests deeper; small starts show two or three levels.

sections.heading: The nested phases, level by level
html: When the single-number map lands on Y(n) with n odd, a second number appears and is run through the same 3/2 rule until a parity test ends the phase. The first two levels are now exact:

nnext single-number eventmoments at the left end
4i+1X(9i+9)5
8i+7X(27i+36)8
8i+3deeper: X(22) from Y(3), Y(119) from Y(27), …9 to 13

The factors 9/4 and 27/8 are (3/2)² and (3/2)³: each level applies the 3/2 rule once more, and how many levels a phase takes depends on how many factors of 2 the numbers contain. Every nested phase from n < 400 comes back without halting.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.066). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.501).
After 109 steps the tape spans 42,324 cells (48 left of the start, 30,497 right), with a density of 1s of 0.502.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

summary: A 3/2 Collatz-like map with nested phases; the nested phases are now exact for n = 4i+1 and 8i+7 (factors 9/4 and 27/8), and every nested phase from n < 400 returns without halting. Open.
